sanskrit_verse:
साक्षिविप्रतिपत्तौ तु प्रमाणं बहवो यतः।
तत्साम्ये शुचयो ग्राह्यास्तत्साम्ये स्मृतिमत्तराः॥
transliteration: sākṣivipratipattau tu pramāṇaṃ bahavo yataḥ | tatsāmye śucayo grāhyās tatsāmye smṛtimattarāḥ ||
sph_interpretive_translation: In the conflict of witness testimony, multiple evidentiary sources exist; when equal, those pure in conduct are to be accepted, and when still equal, those with superior memory.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority derived from purity of action establishes precedence in evidentiary value
Causation flows from inner integrity rather than external corroboration alone
Capacity-based responsibility includes cognitive reliability and spiritual cleanliness
Restoration logic prioritizes alignment with Dharma over adversarial truth-seeking
Consciousness alignment determines admissibility and weight of testimonial evidence
executable_legal_axioms: IF witness testimonies are equally supported by external evidence THEN prioritize testimony of individuals whose conduct history aligns with Dharmic observance
IF testimonial credibility remains equivalent after conduct assessment THEN select testimony based on documented cognitive clarity and memory precision
IF no variance in memory or conduct exists THEN invoke neutral third-party attestation aligned with Nyaya-smriti protocols
ALL evidentiary evaluation MUST exclude punitive bias and orient toward factual reintegration within Dharma
supreme_court_application: At the Supreme Court level, when conflicting testimonies reach equipoise under empirical analysis, judicial discernment shall elevate testimony grounded in a lifelong record of Dharmic conduct. If both witnesses demonstrate equal moral standing, then preference shall shift to those displaying exceptional mental discipline and accurate recollection capacity, verifiable through past judicial records or expert certification.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa operates through sequential manifestation: first sensory perception, then cognitive processing, finally ethical validation. When testimonial parity arises, śuci (purity) functions as the next causal layer, not punitive suspicion. This progression upholds anupūrvaśaḥ—causal unfolding without blame. Responsibility lies in aligning testimony with consciousness, not in extracting penalty from error.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate Śuddhi Vidhi (purification protocol) for all involved witnesses to restore neutrality and remove subconscious distortions
Deploy Smriti Sthapana (memory establishment technique) using guided recall methods to enhance accuracy without coercion
Establish Samyama Adhikara Panel—a panel of spiritually advanced observers—to assess conduct-based credibility without punitive judgment
Implement Vak Yoga Completion Process wherein witnesses reaffirm alignment between speech and consciousness until integration is verified
final_declaration: By the Source-Authority of the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands executed: witness conflict resolves through purity, memory, and consciousness—not punishment. Dharma prevails; reality remains non-punitive; consciousness is the ultimate judge.
